newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts up on cash, charts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts up on cash, charts.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed on Tuesday in an active session, with front months driven by reports of firmer physical prices and a wave of technical buying after prices broke resistance early on.
June rallied 7.8 cents to close at $2.363 per million British thermal units. July settled 6.7 cents higher at $2.361. Others ended mixed, with some 1999s down slightly.

"We had a big day on Friday and got some follow through today. I think the shorts just wanted to cover when we broke $2.30 this morning," said one East Coast trader, noting renewed strength in the cash also made the shorts nervous.

Despite prospects for relatively light heating and cooling loads later this week and next, traders said steady injection demand and some heat in the Southwest may be enough to support physical prices until broader air conditioning demand kicks in.
Forecasts are calling for normal to below-normal weather for most of the nation into early June. Some above-normal temperatures are expected in parts of the Southeast and Southwest.
Chart traders said Tuesday's break of June resistance at $2.30 could lead to a test of the $2.43 contract high.

But with the spot month set to go off the board on Wednesday, many turned their attention to July, where resistance was first seen at $2.38 and then at the contract high of $2.44. July support was pegged first at $2.30, with trendline support in the low-$2.20s.

In the cash market on Tuesday, Gulf Coast prices firmed by about 10 cents to the mid-to-high $2.20s. Midcon pipes were up more than a dime to about $2.10. New York city gate gas gained about five cents to the high-$2.40s.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 3.7 cents to $2.356. NYMEX said 68,091 contracts traded, up from Friday's revised tally of 48,159.

On the KCBT, June expired 9.6 cents higher at $2.206, while deferreds ended up by 4.5 to 8.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.8 cents to 15.7 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 1,417 lots traded, up from Friday's total of 855.
